messages:
alex: quick heads-up—i'm about to hand off primary to @mira in 10m. current context: increased 5xxs on embed-serving (region: us-west-2) since 03:10 UTC, but degraded error-rate is ~0.8% above our SLO window. see incident-bot thread for alerts.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1421 — embed-serving 5xx spike (us-west-2). Pager rule: p1->primary, p2->secondary.

mira: on it, thanks alex. do we have a mitigation plan or are we still triaging? any immediate rollbacks?

alex: triaging. initial quick mitigation was to enable fallback shard routing to v1-small-model which has lower qps but stable. i pushed a temporary routing policy at 03:16 UTC.

alex: command used:```sh
redwoodctl routing set --service embed-serving --policy fallback:v1-small --ttl 30m --reason "oncall temp routing due to 5xx spike"
```

devon: noted. that routing change reduced 5xx rate from ~3.2% -> ~1.1% over 2 minutes. still above our slo (0.5% 5xx).

jess: customer-impact check: only non-enterprise tenants in us-west-2 saw errors; no billing or data loss. Affected estimates: ~120 unique API keys. I've opened a quick ticket for support triage.

mira: thanks. handoff: i'm taking primary at 03:25 UTC. devon you stay secondary?

devon: i can stay secondary until 07:00 UTC, then jess will cover.

mira: good. two operational asks before i go full primary: 1) can we suppress noisy low-priority alerts for 10m so paging doesn't wake peeps for transient flaps, and 2) do we want to temporarily relax SLO alert threshold so we avoid auto-escalation?

alex: i already suppressed the rate-based alert on embed-serving/error-rate-low using the alert manager for 15m at 03:20. command:```yaml
/alert-suppress add --alert "embed-serving.error_rate_5xx" --duration 15m --owner "alex" --reason "handoff temp suppression"
```

ops-bot: Alert suppression active: embed-serving.error_rate_5xx — expires in 14m 40s — initiated by alex.

mira: for SLO relax — i'm proposing a controlled threshold bump from 0.5% -> 1.0% on the severity->page rule for the next 30m, explicitly documented in the incident. this avoids auto-pager storm while we stabilize with fallback routing. thoughts?

devon: i'm wary of policy changes mid-incident, but given fallback reduced errors and impact limited to non-enterprise, temporary bump seems reasonable if we: a) record the change, b) set strict expiry, c) post in #incidents for visibility.

jess: agree with devon. i'll update support ticket and customer comms template if we escalate. also, add runbook reference in case we need to scale dedicated pool: runbook link -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embed-serving#scale-dedicated

mira: doing it now. command to adjust alert threshold:```json
{
  "service": "embed-serving",
  "alert": "error_rate_pager",
  "old_threshold": "0.5",
  "new_threshold": "1.0",
  "duration": "30m",
  "author": "mira",
  "reason": "temporary threshold bump during on-call handoff and fallback routing"
}
```

ops-bot: Alert configuration updated: error_rate_pager for embed-serving — threshold set to 1.0% for 30m (expires 03:55 UTC). Change recorded in audit log AL-98765.

alex: note for the handoff log: primary -> mira at 03:25 UTC, suppression & threshold bump applied. fallback routing remains active TTL 30m (expires 03:46 UTC).

mira: confirmed i'm primary. devon you'll be secondary. jess will pick up after 07:00. i'll run a quick synthetic check and keep an eye on customer error groups.

devon: i'll monitor metrics dashboards and be ready to escalate if error rate rises above 2% even with suppression (manual page).

jess: support will queue the impacted tenants and start outreach if errors persist beyond 30m.

mira: launching quick synthetic load test to validate fallback path. log snippet:```text
[03:28:14] synthetic-check embed-serving -> 200 OK (latency 120ms)
[03:28:15] synthetic-check embed-serving -> 500 (backend timeout)
[03:28:17] synthetic-check embed-serving -> 200 OK (latency 140ms)
```

mira: early signs are mixed but trending down. i'll extend the routing fallback if needed; will not extend the SLO bump without group consent. posting this entire thread to #incidents for visibility.

ops-bot: Message posted to #incidents by mira.

alex: thanks team. i'll make a brief post-incident note in the handoff doc once we confirm stability. next steps: keep suppression and threshold change until TTL expiry, monitor, and decide on permanent mitigation (rollback model push or scale pool).

mira: agreed. i'm taking the bridge if this escalates. ping me @mira directly for pages.

devon: noted. good handoff. :thumbsup:

jess: thanks — support on standby.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1421 status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Primary: mira. Secondary: devon. Audit: AL-98765.

mira: closing thread for now, will update if anything changes.
